{{marriage|[[Simone Tata|Simone Dunoyer]]|1955}} | children = 3, including [[Ratan Tata|Ratan]] and [[Noel Tata|Noel]] | parents = [[Ratanji Tata]] (adoptive father) | relatives = See [[Tata family]] | awards = }} '''Naval Hormusji Tata''' (30 August 1904 – 5 May 1989) was an Indian industrialist and philanthropist who worked for the [[Tata Group]]. He was the adopted son of [[Ratanji Tata|Sir Ratan Tata]], and the father of [[Ratan Tata|Ratan]], Jimmy and [[Noel Tata]]. ==Early life== Naval was born in Surat on 30 August 1904 to a middle-class [[Parsi]] family. His father, Hormusji Tata, belonged to a distant branch of the extended Tata family. Hormusji's grandfather, Navroji Tata, was the second-cousin of [[Jamsetji Tata]]. Both of them are descended from Bhika Tata. Thus, he was a Tata by birth.{{Cite web |title=Ratan Tata, Noel Tata and their lineage to Tata Group founder Jamshedji Tata |url=https://parsikhabar.net/news/ratan-tata-noel-tata-and-their-lineage-to-tata-group-founder-jamshedji-tata/29512/ |access-date=2024-11-10 |website=Parsi Khabar |date=5 November 2024 |language=en-US}} His mother was Ratanbai [[Birth name#Maiden and married names|née]] Rao, daughter of Cooverbai Rao [[Birth name#Maiden and married names|née]] Daboo, the sister of Hirabai Tata [[Birth name#Maiden and married names|née]] Daboo, wife of [[Tata group]] founder [[Jamsetji Tata]].{{Cite web |title=Who is Ratan Tata and how 'real' a Tata is he? |url=https://www.vccircle.com/who-ratan-tata-and-how-real-tata-he |access-date=2024-05-19 |website=VCCircle |language=en-US}} Hormusji was a spinning master in the Advanced Mills at Ahmedabad and died in 1908{{cite web|title=NAVAL HORMUSJI TATA (1904-1989)|url=http://www.tatacentralarchives.com/history/biographies/16%20nhtata.htm|publisher=TATA CENTRAL ARCHIVES|access-date=22 March 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150102070245/http://www.tatacentralarchives.com/history/biographies/16%20nhtata.htm|archive-date=2 January 2015}} when Naval was only four years old. After Naval's father died, his mother relocated to [[Navsari]], where she struggled to earn for the family. Ratanbai's income was derived from embroidery work. Naval lived at the J. N. Petit Parsi Orphanage to make it easier to raise him. Navajbai, wife of Sir Ratanji Tata, adopted him from the orphanage at the age of 13. Ratanji Tata was his maternal uncle because Naval's maternal grandmother and Ratanji's mother were sisters. Naval later graduated from [[Bombay University]] in Economics and proceeded to [[London]] for a short course in Accounting. He never forgot his past and once remarked: {{blockquote|"I am grateful to God for giving me an opportunity to experience the pangs of poverty, which more than anything (else) moulded my character in later years of my life."}} ==Family== Naval's first wife was Sooni Commissariat; they had two sons, [[Ratan Tata|Ratan]] and [[Jimmy Tata]].{{Cite web |last=এক্সপ্রেস |first=বেঙ্গল |date=8 December 2022 |title=দুটা মাত্র ঘর, ব্যাবহার করেন না মোবাইল চিনতে পাচ্ছেন রতন টাটার এই ভাই কে ? |url=https://bengalxpress.in/only-two-houses-dont-use-mobile-phones-can-you-recognize-who-is-ratan-tatas-brother/ |access-date=8 December 2022 |website=Bengal Xpress |language=bn}} Both sons never married or had children. The couple separated in the mid-1940s.{{cite news|title=Ratan Tata rode the tiger economy and now he drives Jaguar|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/comment/personal-view/3556736/Ratan-Tata-rode-the-tiger-economy-and-now-he-drives-Jaguar.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/comment/personal-view/3556736/Ratan-Tata-rode-the-tiger-economy-and-now-he-drives-Jaguar.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|access-date=31 March 2012|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=30 March 2008|location=London|first=William|last=Langley}}{{cbignore}} Naval later married [[Simone Tata|Simone Dunoyer]], a businesswoman from Switzerland, they got married in 1955.{{Cite web|url = http://www.ashacentre.org/index.php?option=com_k2&view=item&id=581:simone-tata&Itemid=3|title = Simone Tata|access-date = 17 December 2014|publisher = The Asha Centre|url-status = dead|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141217182405/http://www.ashacentre.org/index.php?option=com_k2&view=item&id=581:simone-tata&Itemid=3|archive-date = 17 December 2014}} [[Noel Tata]] is their son. ==Career== ===Tata group=== In 1930, he joined the Tata Sons as a despatch clerk-cum-assistant secretary and soon rose to be the Assistant Secretary of Tata Sons Ltd. In 1933, he became the Secretary to the [[Tata Airlines|Aviation Department]] and five years later, he joined as an executive in the Textiles Department. In 1939 he became the Joint Managing Director of the Tata Mills — the controlling company of the [[textile mill]]s run by Tatas and became its managing director in 1947. On 1 February 1941, he became a Director of [[Tata Sons]]. He took over as the managing director of [[Tata Oil Mills Co]] Ltd in 1948. He was also the chairman of the Ahmedabad Advance Mills, a [[Tata Group]] company based at [[Ahmedabad]].The Eastern Economist; a Weekly Review of Indian and International Economic Affairs, Volume 37, Issues 1-1961 Over the years he became chairman of the other [[textile mill]]s and the [[Tata Power|three electric companies]]. From an active director he later became the Deputy Chairman of Tata Sons. He was directly responsible for the management of the three Tata electric companies, the [[Tata Textiles|four textile mills]] and the [[Sir Ratan Tata Trust]].{{cite book|title=India's Industrialists, Volume 1 By Margaret Herdeck, Gita Piramal|date=1985|page=320,321, 436|isbn=9780894104152|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xcbBEHHI-90C&q=naval+h+tata&pg=PA434|access-date=22 March 2015|last1=Herdeck|first1=Margaret|last2=Piramal|first2=Gita|publisher=Three Continents Press }} He was the longest serving colleague and close associate of [[JRD Tata]] on board of [[Tata Sons]]. ===Other companies=== He also served as a director of [[Bank of Baroda]] with Tulsidas Kilachand, [[Rameshwar Das Birla]], Arvind Mafatlal and others.{{cite book|title=Corporate Governance: Concept, Evolution and India Story By Praveen B. Malla|date=2013|page=38|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/exhibition-on-tatas-104083101095_1.html|access-date=22 March 2015}} ===Other activities=== Naval Tata went on to become an internationally recognised authority in labour relations, becoming a member of the [[International Labour Organization]]'s governing body in 1949. His involvement with the International Labour Organisation for over three decades was very fruitful for India. Naval holds the record of being elected to the governing body of the International Labour Organization thirteen times.{{cite book|author=Bakhtiar Dadabhoy|title=Sugar in Milk: Lives of Eminent Parsis|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=h0-5wSwLL5YC&pg=PT145|access-date=22 March 2015|year=2008|publisher=Rupa & Company|isbn=978-81-291-1301-6|pages=145–}} He was founder of ILO's family planning programme. He is author of reports like — In Pursuit of Industrial Harmony: An Employer's Perspective by Naval H. Tata (1976), A Policy for Harmonious Industrial Relations (1980), On Wage Problem and Industrial Unrest by Naval H. Tata, C. V. Pavaskar, B. N. Srikrishna (1982). In 1966, he had been appointed a member of the Labour Panel of the [[Planning Commission (India)|Planning Commission]] set up by the Union Government. He contributed to sports, was associated with a host of other activities, and held senior offices in social, educational and welfare work. He was President of [[Indian Hockey Federation]] for fifteen years and was at helm when Indian hockey team won Olympic Gold in 1948, 1952 and 1956. He served many other institutes like the [[Indian Institute of Science]], the Bombay State Social Welfare Council, Swadeshi League, and the National Safety Council. As a philanthropist, the [[Indian Cancer Society]] was established in 1951 by Naval Tata and Dr. [[Darab Jehangir Jussawala|D. J. Jussawalla]], which is India's first voluntary, non-profit, national organisation for awareness, detection, cure and survivorship of those affected with this disease.{{cite web|title=Indian Cancer Society — Profile|url=http://www.indiancancersociety.org/about-ics/ics-profile.aspx|publisher=Indian Cancer Society|access-date=6 April 2015}} He served as Chairman of the Indian Cancer Society for over 30 years. He was also the President of the Auxiliary Forces Welfare Association and trustee of several philanthropic trusts. He was President of the Employers Federation of India for several years. Having been associated with the organisation for four decades, on his retirement as its president, he was made its "President Emeritus". ==Politics== He differed in opinion with his cousin and long standing colleague, [[J. R. D. Tata|JRD Tata]]. While JRD wanted to steer clear of politics, Naval stood as an [[Candidate|independent candidate]] from [[Mumbai South (Lok Sabha constituency)|South Bombay]] in 1971 but lost elections. ==Awards== Naval was awarded the [[Padma Bhushan]] by the [[President of India]] on Republic Day, 1969.{{cite web |date=2015 |title=Padma Awards |url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |archive-date=2015-10-15 |access-date=21 July 2015 |publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India}} The same year he was given recognition for his role in industrial peace and awarded the ''Sir Jehangir Ghandy Medal''. He was conferred the life membership of the [[National Institute of Personnel Management]]. ==Death== He died on 5 May 1989 due to cancer in [[Bombay]].{{cite book|title=Business Maharajas|page=364,371–73,453–54|url=https://www.google.co.in/search?q=NOEL+TATA+-+TATA+STEEL&ie=utf-8&oe=utf-8&gws_rd=cr&ei=NfIOVbioF4OWuQSO74DgDQ#q=NAVAL++TATA&tbm=bks&start=20|access-date=22 March 2015}}{{cite book|title=Land and People of Indian States and Union Territories: In 36 ..., Volume 16 edited by S. C. Bhatt, Gopal K. Bhargava|date=2006|page=675|isbn=9788178353722|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IleHyBDWbzEC&q=naval+tata&pg=PA675|access-date=22 March 2015 |last1=Bhatt |first1=S.
